findings: Rate samples are bounded to at most one retained point per 250ms in a six-second window, with a 1.5s warmup.
Explicit pause time is excluded; elapsedRealtime includes device sleep. Rates expire after three seconds without bytes.
Worker/sampler publication is synchronized; report callbacks run outside the progress-state lock.
The once-per-second sampler is cancelled when the active operation finishes; there is no idle foreground sampler.
Blocking-call scopes retain actual source/destination/provider identities and unwind in finally blocks.
Verification advances phase bytes without inflating bytes transferred; ZIP cancellation assertions use the verification amount.
Preparation reports inspected counts and does not invent a byte total or ETA.
Source size/change checks, staging cleanup, cancellation stream closure and final publication boundaries remain in place.
Progress reporting does not throw a cancellation check after final publication.
The standalone synthetic provider is separate from shipping app sources, read-only, bounded to eight MiB, and has no network permission.
Narrow panes and enlarged text move named transfer controls below the filename/phase summary; FlowRow wraps controls if needed.
The opt-in grant cleanup bridge uses only the hardcoded owned synthetic provider tree and asserts every unrelated permission is unchanged.
limits: A waiting message identifies an outstanding storage call; it is not a universal provider timeout or proof that a provider has stalled.
Emulator checks do not establish throughput accuracy or background/power behavior on physical tablets.
The new optimized acceptance checker uses only owned synthetic documents and restores all original managed bytes and absences.
